description: Generate API documentation from specification through publishing and maintenance.

steps.description: Write or update the API specification in OpenAPI format.

inputs.name: api-endpoints
inputs.desc: List of API endpoints with methods, paths, and descriptions

inputs.name: data-models
inputs.desc: The request and response data models

outputs.name: openapi-spec
outputs.desc: The OpenAPI 3.x specification document

outputs.name: spec-validation-results
outputs.desc: Validation results confirming the spec is valid and complete

process: Write the info section (title, version, description, contact, license).
Define the paths: each endpoint with method, parameters, request body, responses, and error codes.
Define the components: schemas for request and response objects, security schemes, common parameters.
Validate the spec against the OpenAPI specification and fix any errors.

steps.description: Build request and response examples for each endpoint.

outputs.name: endpoint-examples
outputs.desc: Request and response examples for every endpoint, including error cases

outputs.name: code-snippets
outputs.desc: Code snippets in 3+ languages (curl, Python, JavaScript) for each endpoint

process: For each endpoint, write a realistic request example with valid data.
Write the corresponding success response example.
Write error response examples for common error codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500).
Generate code snippets in curl, Python, and JavaScript for each endpoint.

steps.description: Write the getting started guide and authentication walkthrough.

outputs.name: getting-started-guide
outputs.desc: Step-by-step guide from account creation to first API call

outputs.name: auth-guide
outputs.desc: Authentication and authorization walkthrough

process: Write the prerequisites (account, API key, development environment).
Walk through authentication: how to get credentials, how to include them in requests.
Walk through making the first API call with a real example.
Cover pagination, rate limits, and error handling basics.

steps.description: Publish the documentation and set up the update process.

outputs.name: published-docs
outputs.desc: The published documentation site with search, navigation, and try-it-out functionality

outputs.name: docs-maintenance-plan
outputs.desc: The plan for keeping docs in sync with code changes

process: Choose the documentation hosting solution (Swagger UI, Redoc, ReadMe, custom).
Generate the documentation site from the spec and supplementary guides.
Set up the CI pipeline to regenerate docs on spec changes.
Document the update process for the team.

description: Design and implement a webhook system from event definition through monitoring.

steps.description: Define the events that trigger webhooks and their payload structure.

inputs.name: system-events
inputs.desc: List of events the system produces that external consumers might need

inputs.name: consumer-needs
inputs.desc: What integrators need to react to

outputs.name: event-catalog
outputs.desc: Catalog of webhook events with name, description, trigger condition, and payload schema

outputs.name: payload-schemas
outputs.desc: JSON schema for each event's payload

process: List every event that could trigger a webhook (resource created, updated, deleted, state changes, threshold crossings).
For each event, define the name (resource.action format: order.created, payment.failed), description, and trigger condition.
Design the payload schema for each event: include the event type, timestamp, resource data, and any relevant metadata.
Define the common envelope (event ID, event type, timestamp, API version) that wraps every payload.

steps.description: Design the subscription management system for webhook consumers.

inputs.name: consumer-needs
inputs.desc: How consumers will subscribe and filter

outputs.name: subscription-api
outputs.desc: API design for creating, listing, updating, and deleting webhook subscriptions

outputs.name: filtering-rules
outputs.desc: How consumers can filter which events they receive (event types, resource IDs, conditions)

process: Design the subscription endpoint: POST /webhooks with target URL, event types, optional filters.
Design the verification flow: send a challenge to the target URL and require a correct response before activating.
Design the filtering mechanism: subscribe to specific event types, specific resources, or conditions.
Design the management endpoints: list subscriptions, update filters, pause, delete.

steps.description: Design the delivery engine with retry logic and security.

outputs.name: delivery-spec
outputs.desc: Delivery specification: timeout, retry schedule, failure handling, signing method

outputs.name: security-spec
outputs.desc: Webhook security specification (HMAC signing, timestamp validation, IP allowlisting)

process: Set the delivery timeout (5 to 30 seconds, depending on the consumer).
Design the retry schedule: exponential backoff (30s, 5m, 30m, 2h, 12h) with max attempts.
Design the HMAC signature: include the signing secret, sign the raw payload, send the signature in a header.
Design the failure handling: disable the subscription after N consecutive failures, notify the owner.

steps.description: Set up monitoring and debugging tools for the webhook system.

outputs.name: monitoring-dashboard
outputs.desc: Dashboard for webhook delivery success rate, latency, retry rate, and failure rate

outputs.name: webhook-system-plan
outputs.desc: The complete webhook system plan covering events, subscriptions, delivery, security, and monitoring

process: Configure the delivery log: every attempt with status code, latency, and any error.
Build the monitoring dashboard: delivery success rate, average latency, retry rate, failure rate by event type.
Set alerts for delivery failure spikes (e.g., success rate drops below 95%).
Provide a replay tool for consumers to request redelivery of missed events.

description: Build an integration testing pipeline for API consumers from test planning through CI integration.

steps.description: Plan the integration test suite: what to test and how.

inputs.name: integration-points
inputs.desc: The systems and services the API integrates with

outputs.name: test-plan
outputs.desc: The test plan: test categories (contract, functional, error handling, performance), test cases per endpoint

outputs.name: test-environment-requirements
outputs.desc: What the test environment needs (mock services, test data, credentials)

process: List every integration point (external APIs, databases, message queues, file systems).
For each endpoint, define test cases: happy path, edge cases, error responses, authentication failures.
Define contract tests: verify the API response matches the documented schema.
Define the test environment requirements: test credentials, mock services, seed data.

steps.description: Write the integration test cases.

inputs.name: test-plan
inputs.desc: The test plan with test cases

outputs.name: test-suite
outputs.desc: The written test suite organized by endpoint and test category

outputs.name: test-data-fixtures
outputs.desc: Test data fixtures for each test case

process: Write contract tests that validate response schemas against the OpenAPI spec.
Write functional tests for each endpoint's happy path.
Write error handling tests (invalid input, missing auth, rate limiting, server errors).
Create the test data fixtures needed for each test case.

steps.description: Configure the test environment with mocks and test data.

outputs.name: environment-config
outputs.desc: The configured test environment (mock service configs, database seeds, environment variables)

outputs.name: environment-setup-script
outputs.desc: Script to stand up the test environment from scratch

process: Configure mock services for external dependencies.
Set up the test database with seed data.
Configure environment variables (API keys, base URLs, timeout settings).
Write the setup script that provisions the environment in one command.

steps.description: Integrate the test suite into the CI pipeline.

outputs.name: ci-configuration
outputs.desc: CI pipeline configuration running integration tests on every PR and deployment

outputs.name: testing-pipeline-plan
outputs.desc: The complete integration testing plan covering tests, environment, CI, and maintenance

process: Configure the CI job: install dependencies, run environment setup, execute tests, report results.
Set the test suite to run on every pull request and before every deployment.
Configure test result reporting (JUnit XML, coverage report, failure notifications).
Document the test maintenance process: who updates tests when the API changes.

description: Design and implement an API versioning strategy from policy through migration tooling.

steps.description: Define the versioning policy: how versions work and what constitutes a breaking change.

inputs.name: api-maturity
inputs.desc: Current state of the API (pre-launch, v1 stable, multiple versions in production)

inputs.name: consumer-base
inputs.desc: Who consumes the API and how sensitive they are to changes

outputs.name: versioning-policy
outputs.desc: The versioning policy: versioning scheme (URL path, header, query param), what is breaking vs. non-breaking, deprecation timeline

outputs.name: breaking-change-definitions
outputs.desc: Catalog of what counts as a breaking change (field removal, type change, required field addition, behavior change)

process: Choose the versioning scheme (URL path /v1/, header Accept-Version, query parameter ?version=1) and justify the choice.
Define what constitutes a breaking change (removing a field, changing a field type, adding a required field, changing error codes).
Define what is non-breaking (adding optional fields, adding new endpoints, adding new enum values).
Set the deprecation timeline (minimum notice period, sunset date, migration support).

steps.description: Design the changelog and communication process for API changes.

outputs.name: changelog-format
outputs.desc: The changelog format: how changes are documented (added, changed, deprecated, removed, fixed)

outputs.name: communication-plan
outputs.desc: How changes are communicated to consumers (changelog, email, dashboard banner, migration guide)

process: Design the changelog format following Keep a Changelog conventions.
Define the communication channels for different change types (non-breaking: changelog only; breaking: email + migration guide).
Set the notice period for breaking changes (minimum 90 days recommended).
Design the deprecation notice format in API responses (Sunset header, Deprecation header).

steps.description: Plan the migration tooling and support for consumers upgrading between versions.

outputs.name: migration-toolkit
outputs.desc: Toolkit for version migration: migration guide template, compatibility shim design, version comparison tool

outputs.name: versioning-strategy-document
outputs.desc: The complete API versioning strategy covering policy, changelog, communication, and migration support

process: Design the migration guide template: what changed, why, how to update, code examples before and after.
Design the compatibility mode: how old versions are served alongside new ones (routing, middleware).
Plan the sunset process: usage monitoring, direct outreach to consumers still on deprecated versions, final shutdown.
Compile the complete versioning strategy document.

description: Configure an API gateway from requirements through deployment and monitoring.

steps.description: Gather requirements for the API gateway configuration.

inputs.name: api-inventory
inputs.desc: List of APIs to route through the gateway

inputs.name: traffic-profile
inputs.desc: Expected traffic patterns (requests per second, peak times, geographic distribution)

outputs.name: gateway-requirements
outputs.desc: Requirements: routing rules, authentication methods, rate limits, CORS, SSL, caching

outputs.name: gateway-selection
outputs.desc: Selected gateway solution with justification (Kong, AWS API Gateway, Nginx, Traefik, custom)

process: List every API and the routing rules needed (path-based, host-based, header-based).
Define the authentication methods to support (API key, OAuth 2.0, JWT, mutual TLS).
Define the rate limiting requirements per consumer tier.
Evaluate gateway options against the requirements and select one.

steps.description: Configure the routing, authentication, and policies.

outputs.name: route-configuration
outputs.desc: The routing configuration mapping external paths to internal services

outputs.name: policy-configuration
outputs.desc: Authentication, rate limiting, CORS, caching, and transformation policies

process: Configure each route: external path to internal service URL, method filtering, path rewriting.
Configure authentication: which routes require which auth method, how credentials are validated.
Configure rate limiting: per-consumer, per-endpoint, with appropriate responses (429 with Retry-After header).
Configure CORS, request/response transformations, and caching policies.

steps.description: Harden the gateway security configuration.

outputs.name: security-configuration
outputs.desc: Security hardening: TLS settings, IP filtering, request size limits, header injection prevention

outputs.name: security-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of security testing against the gateway

process: Configure TLS: minimum TLS 1.2, strong cipher suites, HSTS header.
Configure request size limits to prevent payload-based attacks.
Configure IP allowlisting or blocklisting as needed.
Set security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy).

steps.description: Deploy the gateway and set up monitoring.

outputs.name: deployment-config
outputs.desc: The deployment configuration (infrastructure as code, scaling rules, health checks)

outputs.name: gateway-plan
outputs.desc: The complete API gateway plan covering routes, policies, security, deployment, and monitoring

process: Write the deployment configuration (infrastructure as code if applicable).
Configure auto-scaling rules based on traffic patterns.
Set up health checks for the gateway and upstream services.
Configure the monitoring dashboard: request rate, latency percentiles, error rate, rate limit triggers.

description: Design a rate limiting system from policy through implementation and consumer communication.

steps.description: Design the rate limiting policy and tiers.

inputs.name: consumer-tiers
inputs.desc: The different consumer tiers (free, basic, pro, enterprise)

outputs.name: rate-limit-policy
outputs.desc: Rate limits per tier per endpoint (requests per second, per minute, per day, burst allowance)

outputs.name: limit-algorithm
outputs.desc: The rate limiting algorithm to use (token bucket, sliding window, fixed window) with justification

process: Analyze current traffic patterns to understand normal and peak usage per consumer tier.
Set limits per tier: free tier gets the lowest, enterprise the highest. Include burst allowances.
Choose the rate limiting algorithm (token bucket for smooth traffic, sliding window for accuracy).
Define per-endpoint limits for expensive operations (search, report generation, file upload).

steps.description: Design the response behavior when limits are hit.

outputs.name: response-spec
outputs.desc: How the API responds when limits are hit (429 status, headers, retry guidance, queue option)

outputs.name: header-spec
outputs.desc: Rate limit headers returned on every response (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset)

process: Define the 429 response body: include the limit that was hit, when it resets, and how to request a higher tier.
Define the rate limit headers for every response (not just 429): Limit, Remaining, Reset.
Design the Retry-After header value (seconds until the next window).
Consider a queue or backpressure option for enterprise consumers instead of hard rejection.

steps.description: Implement the rate limiting and document it for consumers.

outputs.name: implementation-spec
outputs.desc: The implementation spec: where limits are enforced (gateway, middleware, application), storage (Redis, in-memory), key format

outputs.name: rate-limiting-documentation
outputs.desc: Consumer-facing documentation explaining the limits, how to check usage, and how to handle 429 responses

process: Decide where to enforce: API gateway (simplest), middleware (more control), or application layer (most flexible).
Choose the storage backend for counters (Redis for distributed, in-memory for single-node).
Define the key format: by API key, by IP, or by consumer ID.
Write the consumer-facing documentation: what the limits are, how to check remaining quota, how to handle 429.

description: Design and implement API key management from generation through rotation and revocation.

steps.description: Write the API key policy covering generation, scoping, and lifecycle.

inputs.name: consumer-model
inputs.desc: How consumers are organized (accounts, projects, environments)

outputs.name: key-policy
outputs.desc: API key policy: format, scoping (per-project, per-environment), permissions model, expiration rules

outputs.name: key-format-spec
outputs.desc: Key format specification (prefix, entropy, encoding, length)

process: Define the key format: prefix for identification (sk_live_, sk_test_), sufficient entropy (256 bits), base62 encoding.
Define the scoping model: keys scoped to projects, environments (live vs. test), and permission sets.
Set expiration rules: maximum lifetime, rotation reminders, grace period after expiration.
Define the permissions model: what each key can access based on its scope.

steps.description: Design the key lifecycle: creation, rotation, and revocation.

outputs.name: lifecycle-flows
outputs.desc: Flows for key creation, rotation (with overlap period), and revocation

outputs.name: audit-trail-spec
outputs.desc: What key events to log (created, used, rotated, revoked, expired) and the log format

process: Design key creation: generate, show once, store hashed.
Design key rotation: create new key, overlap period where both work, deactivate old key.
Design key revocation: immediate disable, grace period option, notification to key owner.
Design the audit trail: log every key event with timestamp, actor, IP, and key prefix (never the full key).

steps.description: Build the self-service key management dashboard for consumers.

outputs.name: dashboard-spec
outputs.desc: Dashboard specification: key list, usage stats, rotation controls, activity log

outputs.name: key-management-plan
outputs.desc: The complete API key management plan covering policy, lifecycle, dashboard, and security practices

process: Design the key list view: name, prefix (last 4 characters), created date, last used, status, permissions.
Design the key creation flow: name the key, select permissions, show the key once with copy button.
Design the usage stats view: requests per key over time, last used endpoint.
Design the rotation and revocation controls with confirmation steps.

description: Generate and maintain client SDKs from an API specification.

steps.description: Define which languages to support and what the SDK should include.

inputs.name: target-languages
inputs.desc: Languages to generate SDKs for (Python, JavaScript, Go, Java, Ruby, etc.)

inputs.name: consumer-needs
inputs.desc: What consumers need from the SDK beyond raw API calls

outputs.name: sdk-requirements
outputs.desc: Requirements per language: HTTP client, authentication handling, error types, pagination helpers, retry logic

outputs.name: sdk-style-guide
outputs.desc: Naming conventions and patterns for each language (following language idioms)

process: For each target language, define the idiomatic patterns (Python: snake_case, type hints; JS: camelCase, Promises).
Define the SDK features beyond raw calls: authentication wrappers, pagination iterators, retry with backoff, typed errors.
Define the packaging and distribution method for each language (PyPI, npm, Maven, etc.).
Define the minimum supported language versions.

steps.description: Configure the SDK generator and customize the output.

outputs.name: generator-config
outputs.desc: Generator configuration (OpenAPI Generator, Speakeasy, or custom) with templates and customizations

outputs.name: generated-sdks
outputs.desc: The generated SDK code for each target language

process: Select the generator (OpenAPI Generator, Speakeasy, Stainless, or custom templates).
Configure the generator for each language: package name, namespace, authentication handling.
Customize templates for language-idiomatic patterns where the default output is not sufficient.
Generate the SDK code and review the output.

steps.description: Write tests for the generated SDKs.

outputs.name: sdk-tests
outputs.desc: Test suite for each SDK: unit tests, integration tests, example scripts

outputs.name: sdk-examples
outputs.desc: Example code showing common use cases in each language

process: Write unit tests for authentication, error handling, pagination, and retry logic.
Write integration tests against a test API instance.
Write example scripts showing the most common 5 to 10 use cases.
Verify each SDK installs from its package manager and runs the examples.

steps.description: Plan the SDK release process and versioning.

outputs.name: release-process
outputs.desc: The release process: version bumping, changelog, package publishing, announcement

outputs.name: sdk-plan
outputs.desc: The complete SDK plan covering generation, testing, release, and maintenance

process: Define the versioning scheme (semantic versioning, tied to API version).
Set up the CI pipeline: on API spec change, regenerate SDKs, run tests, publish if tests pass.
Define the release checklist: update changelog, bump version, publish to package registry, update docs.
Document the maintenance process: who monitors issues, response time, backport policy.

description: Manage the lifecycle of deprecating and sunsetting API features or versions.

steps.description: Assess the impact of deprecating an API feature or version.

inputs.name: deprecation-target
inputs.desc: What is being deprecated (endpoint, field, version, feature)

inputs.name: usage-data
inputs.desc: Current usage data for the target (consumers, request volume, growth trend)

outputs.name: impact-assessment
outputs.desc: Number of affected consumers, request volume at risk, and business impact estimate

outputs.name: migration-complexity
outputs.desc: Complexity assessment: is there a drop-in replacement, or does the consumer need to rewrite logic?

process: Pull usage data for the deprecation target: how many consumers, how many requests, trending up or down.
Identify the top consumers by volume and assess their likely migration effort.
Determine if a replacement exists and how different it is from the deprecated feature.
Estimate the migration complexity (drop-in replacement, minor changes, significant rewrite).

steps.description: Write the deprecation plan with timeline and communication.

inputs.name: migration-complexity
inputs.desc: How hard it is for consumers to migrate

outputs.name: deprecation-plan
outputs.desc: The plan: deprecation announcement date, migration period length, sunset date, support during migration

outputs.name: migration-guide
outputs.desc: The consumer-facing migration guide (what changed, how to update, before/after code examples)

process: Set the deprecation timeline: announcement, migration period (minimum 90 days for breaking changes), sunset date.
Write the migration guide: what is deprecated, what replaces it, code examples showing the change.
Plan the communication: changelog entry, email to affected consumers, API response headers (Deprecation, Sunset).
Plan the support during migration: office hours, dedicated support channel, proactive outreach to top consumers.

steps.description: Execute the deprecation and monitor adoption of the replacement.

outputs.name: migration-tracking
outputs.desc: Tracking data: consumers migrated vs. remaining, usage on deprecated vs. replacement

outputs.name: deprecation-report
outputs.desc: The complete deprecation report covering announcement, migration, sunset, and lessons learned

process: Publish the deprecation announcement and add Deprecation and Sunset headers to API responses.
Track migration progress: percentage of consumers migrated, traffic shift from deprecated to replacement.
Proactively contact consumers who have not migrated as the sunset date approaches.
Execute the sunset: return 410 Gone on the deprecated feature, compile the deprecation report.

description: Set up API monitoring from metric definition through alerting and incident response.

steps.description: Define the API metrics to monitor.

inputs.name: sla-targets
inputs.desc: The SLA targets (uptime, latency, error rate)

outputs.name: metric-definitions
outputs.desc: Defined metrics: request rate, latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99), error rate by code, availability

outputs.name: sli-slo-mapping
outputs.desc: SLIs mapped to SLOs for each API (e.g., p99 latency under 500ms, error rate under 0.1%)

process: Define the golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation.
For each API, set the SLIs (what to measure) and SLOs (what targets to hit).
Define the latency percentiles to track (p50 for typical, p95 for slow, p99 for worst case).
Define the error rate breakdown (by HTTP status code, by error type).

steps.description: Build the monitoring dashboard.

outputs.name: dashboard-layout
outputs.desc: The dashboard layout: overview panel, per-API detail, error drill-down, latency heatmap

outputs.name: dashboard-config
outputs.desc: The dashboard configuration for the monitoring tool (Grafana, Datadog, CloudWatch, etc.)

process: Design the overview panel: total request rate, overall error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, SLO burn rate.
Design per-API panels: request rate, latency, error rate, top callers.
Design the error drill-down: error rate by endpoint, by status code, with example error messages.
Design the latency heatmap: latency distribution over time to spot regressions.

steps.description: Configure alerts for SLO violations and anomalies.

inputs.name: sli-slo-mapping
inputs.desc: The SLIs and SLOs to alert on

outputs.name: alert-rules
outputs.desc: Alert rules: thresholds, evaluation windows, severity levels, notification channels

outputs.name: runbook-stubs
outputs.desc: Runbook stubs for each alert (what it means, likely causes, first steps)

process: Configure SLO-based alerts: alert when the error budget burn rate is too fast (multiwindow, multi-burn-rate).
Configure threshold alerts for immediate issues: error rate above 5%, p99 latency above 5 seconds.
Set severity levels: warning (investigate), critical (page on-call), emergency (all hands).
Write a runbook stub for each alert: what it means, common causes, first diagnostic steps.

steps.description: Plan the incident response process for API outages.

outputs.name: incident-response-plan
outputs.desc: The incident response plan: roles, communication, escalation, postmortem

outputs.name: api-monitoring-plan
outputs.desc: The complete API monitoring plan covering metrics, dashboards, alerts, and incident response

process: Define the incident roles: incident commander, communications lead, technical lead.
Define the communication plan: status page updates, consumer notification, internal updates.
Define the escalation path: when to escalate from on-call to team lead to engineering leadership.
Define the postmortem process: timeline, root cause analysis, action items, follow-up.
